A digital marketplace designed to connect plastic waste collectors, aggregators, recyclers and manufacturers has been introduced in Ghana to improve trading and strengthen plastic waste recovery.
The DigiPlas-GH platform is expected to provide a virtual marketplace where stakeholders can buy and sell recyclable materials, access market opportunities and coordinate activities across the plastic waste value chain.
The platform will also help track the volume and quality of plastic waste collected and channelled into recycling, providing data to assess the impact of recovery activities.
Speaking at a stakeholder engagement workshop at the KNUST Engineering Guest House in Kumasi, Senior Research Scientist at the CSIR-Institute of Industrial Research, Engineer Dr Latifatu Mohammed, said the initiative would make it easier for collectors and recyclers to trade.
“DigiPlas-GH platform is a marketplace where recyclers and collectors, plastic waste value chain stakeholders, can actually come together to sell and buy,” she emphasised.
She said the platform would also provide information on the amount of plastic waste generated, collected and recovered.
“Aside from that, we also want to use that platform to know how much we are generating and how much we are collecting, how much we are impacting the environment by our activities in the waste plastic value chain,” she said.
Engineer Dr Mohammed said the platform was expected to address challenges in the sale of recovered plastics and the sourcing of materials by recycling companies.
She explained that introducing standards for the materials traded on the platform would help buyers and sellers establish the weight and quality of plastic waste and reduce disputes over transactions.
“If we are able to put standards to the plastic that is collected, be able to tell you the weight I have collected, the quality of the plastic, then I know I'm getting the exact amount that merits the quantity I have collected,” she said.
The marketplace is also expected to reduce reliance on physical market arrangements by allowing users to identify buyers and suppliers and conduct transactions remotely.
“Here is a virtual platform where you can sit in the comfort of your home and trade, and if I also want to buy, I can easily go there in the comfort of my home, source and then buy, and then it's delivered to me,” she explained.
The initiative is being piloted in Accra, Kumasi and Takoradi, selected because of their large populations. The project could be extended to other regions after the pilot, depending on its success.
Engineer Dr Mohammed said consultations with stakeholders were important to ensure the platform reflects the practical needs of those involved in plastic waste recovery.
“Stakeholder engagement is really important because you are engaging them to get their view to help develop their platform that will be usable to them,” she said.
The project is being implemented by the CSIR-Institute of Industrial Research in collaboration with the CSIR-Science and Technology Policy Research Institute (CSIR-STEPRI) and other partners.
It is funded by the Basel Convention on the Control of Transboundary Movements of Hazardous Wastes and their Disposal, with funding administered by the United Nations Environment Programme.
A steering committee comprising relevant institutions, including the Environmental Protection Agency, the Ministry of Environment, Science and Technology (MEST), CSIR-STEPRI and private recycling companies such as Zoomlion, is expected to support the project's implementation and long-term sustainability.
The stakeholder workshop was organised to introduce the initiative, identify operational challenges in the plastic waste value chain and gather recommendations to guide the development and sustainability of the DigiPlas-GH marketplace.
